findings.title: A stranger's token name, a pool's ticker and a DRep's name kept from running as a CSV formula: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: Drop the `true` that marks a column as free text: the tokens column (activity.ts:228), the pool column (:231) or the DRep column (:232). A stranger sends the wallet a token whose asset name reads `=HYPERLINK("http://x","y")`. It's unlisted, readable and like no listed ticker, so tokenText labels it by that name, and csvName puts the name first in the cell (:158-162). Save as CSV then writes a cell starting with `=`, which a spreadsheet opening the file runs. A pool's ticker or a DRep's name in the user's staking rows works the same way. All three pass `true` today, so nothing is wrong now. The gap: reverting any of the three passes every test, because the formula test builds its case from a note and a detail only (activity.test.ts:995-1004).

(voteOf(network, s) ?? s.drep) : "", true),` became the same without `, true`. Each run: tests/activity.test.ts (the lanes' named test) 55 passed, 0 failed. The 4 other tests importing activity.ts: 94 passed. The rest of activity.ts's import closure plus the 28 tests that read source files as text (48 files): 761 passed. The pinned siblings fail as they should: csvCell's own check (:170) fails activity.test.ts:997, and the note (:230) and detail (:229) flags fail :1003. e2e's CSV check (e2e/extension.spec.ts:1606-1613) reads only the header and the row count.

The press reaches lovejoin-launch-build, which checks them again (lovejoin-launch.ts:247-266, per lane E8a). So each refusal comes after the press instead of before it.
findings.evidence: Mutant: `  const why = !terms\n    ? undefined` became `  const why = true\n    ? undefined`, removing all six checks at once. lovejoin-merged-review.test.ts (named): 41 passed. 3 direct importers: 54 passed. Closure (55): 869 passed. Since removing all six fails nothing, none is pinned on its own, so per-condition mutants weren't run. No e2e test opens Start a pool.

The form then shows and sends 'Bootstrap the pool with 200 boxes' where one deposit takes 64, and the worker refuses it. The most itself is pinned (:3729-3730).
findings.evidence: Mutant: `  const putting = Math.min(Math.max(asked ?? needed, 1), most);` became `  const putting = Math.max(asked ?? needed, 1);`. lovejoin-release-rules.test.ts (named): 18 passed. 26 direct importers: 534 passed. Closure (32): 412 passed. The :3729 and :3730 mutants fail lovejoin-release-rules.test.ts:482 and :484. e2e/extension.spec.ts:3583-3597 types 12, which is within the most.

findings.title: Bring everything back leaving out a session that runs itself, or one holding nothing: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: Drop `!s.auto &&` or `(s.holding?.utxos ?? 0) > 0` from isClaimable. The dApps page's card (Dapps.tsx:218) then offers Bring everything back for a swap that brings itself back, or for a session holding nothing. The worker's claimBuild skips each with its reason (sessions.ts:3330, :3336), so the review has nothing to send. The chain part is pinned (swap-page.test.ts:369).
findings.evidence: Two mutants of `export const isClaimable = (s: SessionView) => s.stage === "open" && !s.auto && !chainGoing(s) && (s.holding?.utxos ?? 0) > 0;`: one without `!s.auto && `, one without ` && (s.holding?.utxos ?? 0) > 0`. Each run: swap-page.test.ts and restore-scan-lovejoin.test.ts (named) 27 passed. 4 other direct importers: 134 passed. Closure (38): 564 passed. e2e/extension.spec.ts:1017-1021 empties a found session's account, but that session ends there, so the stage check hides the card either way.
findings.fix: In swap-page.test.ts beside :369, expect isClaimable to be false for an open session with auto set holding 1 UTxO, and false for an open session holding 0 UTxOs.

notes: Method: four copies of seedelf-platform/, rsynced from TREE, with node_modules symlinked to TREE's. The verifiers' 38 untracked r51-* tests were moved out of each copy before any run, so every result is the committed suite's. Each mutant was checked against TREE before it was applied. Tests then ran in up to three stages, stopping at the first failure: (1) the lanes' named tests; (2) the other tests importing the module directly; (3) the rest of the tests whose static import closure reaches the module, plus the 28 tests that read source files as text. Every run: `systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=0 timeout 40m npx vitest run --maxWorkers=3 --testTimeout=300000 --hookTimeout=300000 --bail=1 --reporter=json`. The copies are removed (no CARGO_TARGET_DIR was used: there were no Rust guards).

Departures from the given commands, said plainly. `nice -n 10` (given for cargo) starved Vitest at load ~70: workers got ~13% of a core, and one 27-file stage ran past 10 minutes. So the Vitest runs went without it, as the brief's TypeScript command has it. A full-suite baseline was started and then stopped: under that load the default 5 s test timeout failed tests (11 in the first ~380), hence the 300 s timeout. Instead of a baseline, every catch in checked_ok was checked to be an assertion on the mutated value (the expected/actual pairs quoted), not a timeout or a flake.

Near-equivalent mutants, put here rather than among the findings because no reachable state shows them. (1) Withdraw.tsx:92 and CardanoSend.tsx:96 readOf's exact-text check: DestinationInput reports {to, read} on every change of its text (Destination.tsx:112), so the record's text matches the field's outside a single render, and the build sends draft.to, which the worker resolves again (destination.ts:41-71). (2) Transfer.tsx:139 pays f.seedelf.name: `found` follows the field's normalized name (Transfer.tsx:436-450), and transfer.ts:186-187 normalizes draft.to the same way, so either pays the same Seedelf. (3) RemoveSeedelf.tsx:197's `!to`: the submit is disabled without a destination (:282), and implicit submission doesn't fire on a disabled default button.

A doubt, too thin for a finding. DestinationInput's report effect runs in the same flush as useDestination's setRead({ state: 'reading' }) (Destination.tsx:56-60, then :112). So the first report after an edit pairs the new text with the previous read, and for one render readOf's text check counts the old read for the new text. A person can't press inside that render in practice, and the build pays the new text.

Not done: (1) Playwright isn't run by this lens, so the 11 e2e-only pins are traced, not run.
